title: CERT-In Vulnerability Note  CIVN-2026-0578
content:
CERT-In Vulnerability Note 
                                                                      CIVN-2026-0578
Memory Management Vulnerability in Linux Kernel KVM
Original Issue Date:November  27, 2026
Severity Rating: HIGH
Software Affected
Linux Kernel versions prior to 5.16, 6.1.193, 6.12.118, 6.18.64, 7.3.5 and 7.4-rc2
Overview
A vulnerability has been identified in the Linux Kernel KVM subsystem which may allow an attacker with privileges inside a guest virtual machine to gain unauthorized read and write access to host memory under specific conditions.
Target Audience:
All end user organizations and individuals using the affected Linux Kernel KVM-based virtualization environments.
Risk Assessment:
High risk of unauthorized access to host memory, compromise of virtual machine isolation, and potential compromise of the host system.
Impact Assessment:
Potential for unauthorized access to host memory, exposure of sensitive information, and compromise of the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of the affected system.
Description
Linux Kernel-based Virtual Machine (KVM) is a virtualization technology that allows Linux systems to function as hypervisors, enabling multiple virtual machines to run on a single physical host.
This vulnerability exists in the Linux Kernel KVM subsystem due to improper handling of the Memory Management Unit (MMU) context while emulating an INIT reset in nested AMD virtualization environments. The issue may result in a stale nested page table pointer due to improper reset of the MMU context.
A local attacker with privileges inside a guest virtual machine could exploit this vulnerability under specific conditions to gain read and write access to host memory, potentially compromising the host system and other virtual machines running on the same physical server.
Solution
Apply appropriate updates as mentioned by the vendor:
https://www.kernel.org/
